## Historical audit — S0077

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/ablation_r1/ours_without_regression_guidance/C1/selection/commons_138420790/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to JSONL lines in this file; observations are not split across chunks.

**Goal versus outcome:** The requested goal was a geometrically and visually faithful reconstruction of a single indoor photograph, including camera and framing (line 1). The observed outcome was three formally successful Blender executions and a final `DONE`, with step 3 selected (lines 5–6, 11–12, 17–18, 21). **Visual correctness remains unknown**: neither the reference nor renders are visible in this audit. Successful execution is not proof of reconstruction accuracy.

| Evidence | Observed operations and limits |
|---|---|
| Initial build, student response and execute, lines 3–4 | Code constructs multiple separate groups: architecture, island, extractor, rear cabinetry, oven bank, kettle and posts. It specifies procedural wood grain and stone bump, colored surfaces, a camera, world and area lights. Island and kettle attachments are grouped hierarchically; support heights are manually specified, without bindings. These are construction facts, not independent proof of visibility, texture appearance or physical contact. |
| First review and revision, lines 7–10 | The student reports render 1 as too distant, the island front too broad relative to its end, and the column overlapping the island. It changes camera position, aim and lens, and moves the foreground post, intending improved framing and parallax. This is the student’s assessment and hypothesis, not an independently verified comparison. |
| Occlusion investigation, lines 13–17 | The student reports that render 2 showed only a pale surface, then hypothesizes that the camera was outside the left wall. Step 3 moves the wall from x = −3.35 to −7 while retaining camera 2 and the other scene groups. Execution succeeds and saves a render; the available text does not independently establish that the wall caused the obstruction or that the final framing improved. |
| Validation and termination, lines 17–21 | Step 3 reports `ok: true`, saves `final.png` and `scene.blend`, and is selected. The student receives the final render in its next request and answers `DONE`; no explanatory final visual assessment is recorded. Logs show 16 render samples despite the program setting 48. |

**Teacher input and autonomy:** No teacher event, diagnosis, proposed update or student adoption of teacher feedback is recorded. The post-render messages are generic runner review instructions, not identified teacher interventions (lines 7, 13, 19). Within those constraints, the student chose the camera/post revision and the subsequent wall-occlusion hypothesis and repair itself. Sessions report no student tool calls (lines 2, 8, 14, 20).

**Lessons and uncertainty:** A transferable observation is that a successful render can still be visually unusable, and checking camera–architecture occlusion can preserve existing objects during repair. The particular wall position and camera are task-specific; the causal diagnosis and success of the repair remain hypotheses here. Actual object visibility, pose, material appearance, light quality, contacts and final reference match cannot be verified from the supplied text alone. No technical interruption or empty patch is evidenced; formal execution success should not be conflated with scene correctness.
